claims.text: Introducing a nanohierarchical architecture with composition undulation will improve the wear resistance of a FeNiCrCoCu high-entropy-alloy coating on a Cu matrix.
A nanohierarchical architecture with composition undulation was deployed in Ni50(AlNbTiV)50.
The proposed modified FeNiCrCoCu coating would be structurally similar to the nanohierarchical Ni50(AlNbTiV)50 alloy.
The architecture would create intrinsically nano-coupled grains and nanoprecipitates in the FeNiCrCoCu coating.
Nano-coupled grains and nanoprecipitates would provide multi-type adaptive friction-interface protection.
The proposed heterostructure would release gradient frictional stress during wear.
The proposed architecture would activate a dense nanocrystalline glaze layer at elevated temperature.
Adaptive interface protection, stress release, and glaze-layer formation would improve the coating's wear resistance.
The modified FeNiCrCoCu coating will have better wear resistance than the unchanged coating under identical test conditions.
The wear rate of the modified coating may be reduced by one order of magnitude relative to the unchanged FeNiCrCoCu coating.
The wear-resistance prediction applies from room temperature to 800 °C.
The wear-resistance prediction applies across different friction velocities.
The wear-resistance prediction applies across different wear depths.
The exact improvement mechanism and optimal nanohierarchical composition and architecture remain uncertain.
Failure to obtain a statistically significant wear-rate reduction relative to the unchanged coating would falsify the hypothesis.

contradictions.description: The mechanism field presents a specific causal sequence as operative, while the uncertainty field says that the exact mechanism is uncertain. This can be reconciled only if the stated mechanism is understood as a tentative proposal rather than an established mechanism.
